text.p: Australian opener Matthew Hayden piled up a career-best 235 not out to spearhead a fightback by his adopted English county Hampshire on Saturday.

Hayden, 81 not out overnight, batted through the third day of the four-day championship match against Warwickshire at Southampton to beat his previous best of 234 for Queensland against Tasmania in the Sheffield Shield.
Hampshire, facing a massive Warwickshire first innings score of 631 for seven declared, were 549 for six at the close.
Hayden, who has batted for 550 minutes and received 414 balls, striking 29 fours and two sixes, figured in two double century stands.
Will Kendall (76) helped Hayden add 206 for the fourth wicket and off-spinner Shaun Udal shared an unbroken seventh wicket partnership of 205 in 45 overs with the Australian.
Udal played the dominant role, hitting a sid and 19 fours in his maiden century and ending the day with an unbeaten 117.

All-rounder Mark Ealham, expected to be named on Sunday in the England squad for the first test against Australia at Edgbaston next week, displayed impressive form as Kent beat Nottinghamshire inside three days at Trent Bridge.

Ealham hit a career-best 122, then held three catches as the home side, second in the county championship table at the start of the match, were skittled out for 119 to lose by an innings and 105 runs.
Lancashire's England captain Mike Atherton hit a timely century ahead of the Ashes series in a high-scoring match against champions Leicestershire at Leicester.
Opener Atherton faced 202 balls and hit 13 fours in making exactly 100 not out as Lancashire, trailing by 95 on first innings, ended the third day on 279 for two.
Yorkshire narrowly failed to beat the clock and become the second side to win with a day to spare, against Essex at Ilford.
Despite claiming an extra half-hour, Yorkshire still needed six more runs with two wickets left to achieve their victory target of 276.

Yorkshire, fired by a fine 81 in 109 balls from Australian Darren Lehmann, reached 229 for three before off-spinner Peter Such checked their charge by taking five for 89. They were 270 for eight at the close.
